summary: Post-market brief. The composite risk score fell 0.45 to 45.23, the risk level stays caution and the regime stays goldilocks; fact-layer confidence is 0.9161. Today's US tape split internally in an unusual way: the AI hardware chain fell across the board -- semiconductor equipment -8.9763%, networking -6.8104%, memory -6.5552%, AI infrastructure -6.4583%, semiconductors -5.6292% and data centers -5.5005% -- while AI software and cybersecurity surged: cybersecurity +5.9852%, enterprise software +5.0433% and AI software +4.1833%. Only 8 of 22 sectors/themes rose while 14 fell. The trigger was the Anthropic chief executive's call that the industry must slow the pace at which it improves model capability, joined by Microsoft setting limits on frontier models; the market repriced the pace of AI capital spending and rotated from compute hardware into software and security. The macro constraint did not ease: the 2-year yield rose to 4.63 from 4.56 and the 10-year to 4.96 from 4.95 (99.92 percentile), the 10-year real rate at 2.6 sits at the 100 percentile, and with the fed funds rate at 3.63 against an implied policy rate of 4.105 a hike is priced. Volatility refused to confirm: the VIX fell to 15.84 from 17.84 with realized volatility at 8.8279, and credit is quiet with HY OAS at 2.65 and IG OAS at 0.8. The A-share memory chain weakened in tandem (688825.SH -3.9485%, 603986.SH -3.8888%, 301308.SZ -2.5151%) while crypto moved the other way (bitcoin at 79530, +2.89719%). Post-market conclusion: this was a narrative-driven re-rating, not a systemic risk event -- a lower risk score, lower volatility and calm credit point to caution rather than deterioration. Breadth remains fragile, though, with 53.55% above the 200-day average and new highs at 1.29% against new lows at 8.39%, and the semis relative strength of -19.1577 is still the widest gap in the tape.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The macro dimension leads the six at 63.83 and is trending rising: the 10-year real rate of 2.6 sits at the 100 percentile (risk score 100.0), the 10-year yield of 4.96 at the 99.92 percentile, the 2-year rose to 4.63 from 4.56 and the 10Y-2Y curve is just 0.33. The long end and the real rate are the only hard constraint right now.

The AI narrative shock gutted hardware: semiconductor equipment -8.9763%, networking -6.8104%, memory -6.5552%, AI infrastructure -6.4583% and data centers -5.5005%, with Nvidia -3.3579%, Broadcom -4.7708%, Micron -5.253% and AMD -4.402%. At the same time cybersecurity +5.9852% and enterprise software +5.0433% absorbed the outflow, which says this is a repricing of pace rather than a retreat from the AI theme as a whole.

Market structure keeps deteriorating: the share above the 200-day average fell to 53.55%, new highs are 1.29% against new lows at 8.39%, small-cap relative strength is -4.3097 and semis relative strength -19.1577. The equity-structure dimension is 53.02 and trending rising, and breadth is the offset inside an otherwise falling score.

A hike is priced: the implied policy rate of 4.105 against an effective fed funds rate of 3.63 has FedWatch pointing to a hike, and both rate strategists and the day's news flow treat a hike this week as the base case, with the odds of another one in December also being discussed. The policy path is the largest event risk after the close.

Within the cross-asset confirmation reading of 0.625, the S&P lower, dollar strength, real-rate pressure, copper lower and small-cap underperformance all triggered, while HY spread widening and gold higher did not -- the cross-asset dimension is flat at 50.0, which says stress is concentrated in rates and inside equities rather than being a broad risk-off.

supporting_signals.claim: Macro and policy are the sole source of upside risk: the macro dimension is 63.83 and trending rising, the 10-year real rate of 2.6 is at the 100 percentile, and the implied policy rate of 4.105 sits above the prevailing 3.63, so the hike pricing is not yet falsified.

The hardware decline has fundamental transmission: the memory theme at -6.5552% moved with the A-share memory chain (688825.SH -3.9485%, 603986.SH -3.8888%, 301308.SZ -2.5151%), and that cross-market consistency says this is not a single-market mood swing.

Breadth and relative strength confirm the divergence: 53.55% above the 200-day average, new highs 1.29% against new lows 8.39%, semis relative strength -19.1577 and small-cap relative strength -4.3097. A small index-level drawdown is masking an internal gap.

The risk score is still in caution territory with a positive monthly trend: total 45.23, weekly trend +2.49, monthly trend +2.66, the trend dimension at 46.32 and rising, price 6.4622 above the 200-day average and the 52-week drawdown only -2.1854 -- the medium-term trend is not yet broken.

contradicting_signals.claim: Volatility refused to confirm: the VIX fell to 15.84 from 17.84 (30.4 percentile), realized volatility is 8.8279 and the volatility dimension is 20.88 and trending falling. A genuine stress event usually comes with volatility rising, and today it did not.

Credit is still quiet: HY OAS at 2.65 (3.95 percentile) and IG OAS at 0.8, with the liquidity and credit dimension at 33.0 and trending falling; reverse repo fell to 1.42 while reserve balances rose to 2991310 -- funding stress is absent.

Risk appetite survives outside of rates: bitcoin at 79530 rose +2.89719% and ether and Solana moved with it, while AI software +4.1833% and cloud computing +2.7134% rising says capital is being reallocated between sectors rather than leaving risk assets.

The inflation and labour mix does not support an escalation in tightening: CPI at 3.35302 and core CPI at 2.44616, below the prior 2.46652, with 5-year and 10-year breakevens down to 2.32 and 2.36 and the unemployment rate flat at 4.1 -- the macro foundation for the hike pricing is not solid.

what_changed_today: The composite risk score fell 0.45 to 45.23, still caution, with the regime unchanged at goldilocks and confidence at 0.9161.
The AI hardware chain was hit hard in one session: semiconductor equipment -8.9763%, networking -6.8104%, memory -6.5552%, AI infrastructure -6.4583% and data centers -5.5005%.
AI software and cybersecurity led against the tape: cybersecurity +5.9852%, enterprise software +5.0433%, AI software +4.1833% and cloud computing +2.7134%.
The long end pushed higher again: the 2-year yield rose to 4.63 from 4.56 and the 10-year to 4.96 from 4.95, taking the 10-year real rate to 2.6 at the 100 percentile.
Volatility and credit both loosened: the VIX fell to 15.84 from 17.84 and HY OAS to 2.65 from 2.7, while bitcoin rose +2.89719% to 79530.
watch_next: US advance retail sales on 2026-09-16 is the nearest high-importance release and will test consumer resilience against a 10-year real rate of 2.6 at the 100 percentile.
The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 is the next policy test, where pricing of an implied policy rate of 4.105 against a fed funds rate of 3.63 will be delivered or overturned.

Whether the AI-slowdown narrative extends: if the declines in semiconductor equipment -8.9763% and memory -6.5552% spread to the wider semiconductor complex, hardware valuations need another leg down.
Whether cybersecurity +5.9852% and enterprise software +5.0433% can keep absorbing flows -- if software follows hardware lower, this was broad risk-off rather than rotation.
Whether credit finally confirms: HY OAS widening from 2.65 or IG OAS rising from 0.8 is the most important missing confirmation in the risk case, alongside FDX earnings on 2026-09-17.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the narrative shock is absorbed while credit and volatility stay calm
points: The volatility dimension is 20.88 and trending falling, with the VIX at 15.84 in the 30.4 percentile and realized volatility at 8.8279, so the hardware sale did not become index-level stress.
No credit stress: HY OAS at 2.65 in the 3.95 percentile and IG OAS at 0.8, with the liquidity and credit dimension at 33.0 and trending falling.
Capital stayed in the market: AI software +4.1833%, cybersecurity +5.9852% and cloud computing +2.7134% absorbed the outflow, and bitcoin at 79530 rose +2.89719%.
The medium-term trend is intact: price is 6.4622 above the 200-day average, the 52-week drawdown is only -2.1854 and 3-month momentum is 2.579.

base_case.title: Base case: rotation continues while rates stay restrictive
points: The composite risk score holds in caution territory at 45.23 with the regime at goldilocks and fact-layer confidence at 0.9161.
The macro constraint is unchanged: the 10-year real rate of 2.6 at the 100 percentile, the 10-year yield at 4.96 and an implied policy rate of 4.105 above the fed funds rate of 3.63.
Index flat with internal rotation: 8 of 22 sectors/themes rose and 14 fell, breadth at 53.55%, new highs 1.29% against new lows 8.39%.
The hardware-software split converges to a new equilibrium, awaiting direction from retail sales on 2026-09-16 and the FOMC on 2026-09-28.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the breadth gap widens and the hardware decline spills over
points: Breadth is already fragile: 53.55% above the 200-day average, new highs 1.29% against new lows 8.39% and semis relative strength at -19.1577.
If the hardware decline spills over, the repricing of memory at -6.5552% and semiconductor equipment at -8.9763% transmits into capex expectations and data centers at -5.5005%.

Delivery of the hike is itself a shock: with the implied policy rate at 4.105 against a fed funds rate of 3.63, if the FOMC on 2026-09-28 delivers, the 10-year yield of 4.96 and the real rate of 2.6 still have room higher.
Once credit confirms -- HY OAS widening from 2.65 or IG OAS rising from 0.8 -- caution migrates toward the risk zone.
